passage: Sunday night. Sangeeta took three hours to reply to my text and I caught myself thinking, Dev would have called. Then I stopped. Dev did not call, most weeks. He sent long, beautiful messages on good days and vanished on the bad ones. I have kept the good days on a shelf in my head and thrown the rest away. Sangeeta, meanwhile, remembers my mother's birthday and turns up with soup when I am ill. That is a real person, not a highlight reel. What I actually want is a little more contact through the workday, and I have never said so. Tomorrow I will tell Sangeeta, calmly, that a quick afternoon check-in text would make me happy. Lakshmi

qa.q: Why did Lakshmi stop the thought that Dev would have called?
qa.a: Lakshmi had felt impatient at the three-hour wait, then realised the memory was edited: Dev often vanished on bad days, so the comparison was unfair.

qa.q: What will Lakshmi say to Sangeeta tomorrow?
qa.a: That a quick afternoon check-in text would be welcome, said calmly.

qa.q: How might Sangeeta feel if Lakshmi never mentions this need?
qa.a: Sangeeta might not know anything is missing, since Lakshmi has never said so.

grounding: The protagonist compares a partner with an ex, sees the ex memory is edited, appreciates the partner and plans to state a need honestly.

passage:
In their Dadar flat, Bhavna was carefully planning the Saturday grocery list, and Vijay caught himself thinking about Ritika. Ritika, who used to wake him at midnight to drive to Marine Drive for chai. Ritika, who never made lists.

It kept happening. Bhavna suggested a quiet dinner; he thought, Ritika would have picked a rooftop party. He felt restless and vaguely dissatisfied, and then guilty.

One evening he remembered, sharply, the other side of Ritika: cancelled plans, the months when she didn't call, the night he waited three hours at the station. His memory had kept only the midnight chai.

Bhavna came in with two cups. She had noticed his headache and made ginger tea without being asked. He looked at her properly for the first time in weeks.

"Bhavna, can I say something? I love how steady you are. And sometimes I miss doing something unplanned. Could we try one surprise evening a month?"

She laughed. "I'll put it on the list."

qa.q: What did Ritika use to wake Vijay up for?
qa.a: She used to wake him at midnight to drive to Marine Drive for chai.

qa.q: What was Vijay feeling as he compared Bhavna with Ritika?
qa.a: Vijay felt restless and dissatisfied, and then guilty for comparing.

qa.q: How did Vijay handle his comparison wisely?
qa.a: He remembered the painful parts his memory had edited out, noticed Bhavna's real strengths, and honestly asked for one unplanned evening a month.

qa.q: How does Bhavna respond to Vijay's request?
qa.a: Bhavna responds with warm humour, happy to try and teasing that she'll add it to her list.

grounding: The passage shows a young man comparing his partner with an ex's highlight reel, who sees that memory is edited, appreciates present strengths and speaks honestly about his needs.

passage:
"You're quiet again," Shreya said, sitting beside Mohit on the sofa.

"Just tired."

"Mohit."

He sighed. "Okay. This is going to sound bad. Sometimes I compare you with Sonam."

Shreya went still. "Go on."

"She and I used to talk for hours about books. You and I mostly talk about work and your mother's knee. And I start thinking, it was better then."

"Was it?"

Mohit paused. "No. That's the thing. I remember the book talks. I forget she mocked my job, and that we broke up because she never wanted to plan anything with me. I'm comparing you with the good bits of her."

Shreya exhaled slowly. "That hurt to hear. But thank you for being honest."

"You're kinder than she was. You show up. I just miss real conversations sometimes."

"Then let's have them. Sunday mornings, no phones. You pick the first book."

He smiled, relieved. "Deal."

qa.q: What did Mohit and Sonam used to talk about?
qa.a: They used to talk for hours about books.

qa.q: How did Shreya feel when Mohit admitted comparing her with Sonam?
qa.a: Shreya was hurt at first, going still, but grateful for his honesty.

qa.q: What did Mohit realise, and what did he ask for?
qa.a: He realised he was comparing Shreya with an edited memory of Sonam, so he named her real strengths and asked honestly for more real conversations.

qa.q: How did Mohit feel at the end of the talk?
qa.a: Mohit felt relieved that being honest led to a plan instead of a fight.

grounding: A dialogue shows a young man comparing his partner with his ex, who sees his memory is edited, appreciates her present strengths and speaks honestly about what he needs.
